paths did not honour it.

  not named _id, mirroring what its exclusion branch already did

An untagged slice, map or nested struct was classified as a relation by its Go
type and skipped. Mongo builds its writes from that metadata but decodes reads
with the bson decoder, so the field was dropped from every document r3 wrote
while still reading back fine - a one-way round trip that only surfaced when
another process re-read the document.

Scope a many-to-many relation to part of its join table

A join table carrying a discriminator column (role, relation, kind) can now
back several relations, declared as `where:<column>=<value>` on the relation
tag or `r3.RelationWhere` on a relation spec.

- Reads filter on the constant and writes both filter and supply it, so a
  relation only ever touches its own slice: two relations over one join table
  no longer delete each other's rows on save
- GORM: preload, join-table sync, Has/HasNo lowering, relation aggregation
- Mongo: the spec-declared form on its filter and aggregate paths
- A relation without the predicate emits exactly the statements it did before
